_comment: Which file from which APPROVED pack becomes which sprite in the game. apply-art-mapping.ps1 reads this, and refuses to copy from any pack whose LICENSE_REGISTRY.json status is not APPROVED - the section 8 gate enforced in code, not just in prose.

targets.why: Buttons were an Image with NO sprite at all - a hard-cornered solid rectangle, which reads as unfinished next to the Kenney art around it. The depth_flat variant has a bottom lip that makes a button look pressable, and being flat it survives being 9-sliced and tinted. Rectangle over round because the labels are words (Restart, Home, Shop), not icons.

Green marks the primary action on each screen and the shop's buy/equip controls, giving the most important next step a consistent positive cue. It uses the same depth_flat rectangle as the blue fallback so every button keeps the same silhouette and pressable bottom lip.

Yellow identifies the shop action, tying it to the game's gold coin economy without competing with green primary actions. The matching depth_flat rectangle keeps the colour semantic while preserving the established button shape.

Red is reserved for close and other stop-or-exit actions, making those controls distinct from progression and purchase actions. Using the same depth_flat rectangle keeps the warning role readable without introducing a different visual style.

Grey provides a quiet treatment for secondary and disabled actions so they sit behind green primary controls in the visual hierarchy. It retains the same depth_flat geometry, allowing state and priority to change without changing button dimensions.

deliberatelyNotMapped.why: The gravity zone is a translucent gameplay REGION marker, not a physical object. A flat translucent purple tint communicates 'the rules are different in here' better than any of the pack's illustrated sprites would, and it tiles cleanly at any size. Substituting art here would be change for its own sake.

The main character is 도리, defined by the user's own reference images in Assets/Common/Character/SourceImage/. A Kenney character sprite was briefly mapped here and then removed on the user's instruction: the shared character across Game01-Game10 must be theirs, not a stock alien. PrefabGenerator already uses this path when a sprite exists, so dropping a 도리 sprite in is all that is needed - no code change.

queued.why: Biggest remaining visual gap. The level itself still has no background art - the sky is a generated vertical gradient behind the camera (UiSpriteGenerator) and nothing else. Using the pack needs a ParallaxBackground component first, which does not exist yet, so this is a coding task and not a file copy. The licence is already APPROVED, so nothing is waiting on that.

Coin magnet and red skin are text-only rows. The mock-up draws an icon well beside each, and CreateShopRow leaves room for one, but no icon file is mapped yet - the approved pack's icons are UI glyphs (check, cross, gear) rather than item art, so this needs a decision about where item icons come from before anything is copied.

_queued_note: 'UI buttons and panels' used to sit here and was removed on 2026-09-02 once it was actually done: button.png is a real target above, SharedArtImporter carries its measured 9-slice border, and the cards/pills are generated by UiSpriteGenerator. Leaving it queued made the dashboard report finished work as still waiting.

_retired_targets._why: ground.png, obstacle.png and coin.png were Kenney sprites copied here by apply-art-mapping.ps1. On 2026-09-08 the owner supplied a night platformer pack and those three were replaced by it. The mapping entries are removed rather than left in place because apply-art-mapping.ps1 copies on every run - leaving them would silently put the Kenney art back the next time anyone ran it, and the revert would look like a bug rather than a mapping.
